The show said the Knicks offense has consolidated around Brunson and Karl-Anthony Towns, with Brunson at about a 33% usage rate and a 32% assist rate. The show said every other Knicks rotation player is under one DK point per minute, with OG Anunoby at about 0.9, Josh Hart at about 0.8 and Mikal Bridges at about 0.7.

Jalen Duren (hamstring) and Isaiah Joe (hip) are out again. Daniss Jenkins started Monday and played 36 minutes, and Kevin Huerter has played 33 and 35 minutes off the bench in the two games without Joe.
He is ruled out tonight (right hamstring strain). Reed starts at center and had 19 points and 11 rebounds in 26 minutes when Duren left Friday.
Detroit is without Jalen Duren and Duncan Robinson at Atlanta, which keeps Paul Reed as the main center minutes off the bench, and Cade Cunningham is probable with knee soreness.
Duren is out again tonight at Orlando with a right hamstring strain. The show said he seems like he might be back soon and mentioned seeing that he could go to the G League first.

Duren (hamstring) and Duncan Robinson (quadriceps) are both out again at Orlando, and Cade Cunningham is probable with knee soreness. John Collins starts at center, Paul Reed splits those minutes off the bench, and Isaiah Joe played 26 minutes on Sunday.

The show said Phoenix will keep giving Jalen Green a big opportunity despite calls for Collin Gillespie or Jordan Goodwin to start, partly because he missed most of last season with a hamstring injury. He has started every game this month, and his minutes have risen lately, topping out at 37 minutes on 11/23.
He is questionable with a left ankle sprain, which would push more minutes to Atlanta's wings and to Kingston Flemings, who is back from a one-game suspension.
He missed his second straight game Wednesday with a sprained left ankle. Kingston Flemings started and CJ McCollum came off the bench.
He is questionable Friday against Washington with a left ankle sprain after missing two straight games, with a back-to-back Saturday.

Jalen Johnson has played 34 to 40 minutes in each of his last four games, so his minutes are secure. The show said his shooting has been poor, including 18% from three, and that the slow-paced 11/20 matchup with Charlotte limits the rebound-and-push game he needs for a ceiling.
The show expects Jalen Johnson to take the other big share of Atlanta's ball handling with McCollum and Flemings out. The show called him always playable with a very high ceiling.

Atlanta has six players out at Oklahoma City, including CJ McCollum and Kingston Flemings, so the ball handling falls to Jalen Johnson, Dyson Daniels and RayJ Dennis. Asa Newell had toe surgery Tuesday and will be re-evaluated in about four months.

Jalen Slawson played 14 minutes and had three blocks after Rick Carlisle removed Jay Huff and Jarace Walker from the rotation, as both played only one minute. The show likes Slawson and said that if he ever got 30-minute starter's run he would be a top-70 fantasy player.

Jalen Slawson played 20 minutes off the bench on 11/23 with Aaron Nesmith out, up from 12 to 14 in his previous three games. The show said he played well but that Indiana still is not giving him enough minutes to be a must-roster player.
Jalen Smith bent back fingers on his left hand in Friday's overtime win but plans to try to play tonight at Minnesota. Norman Powell returned from back spasms with no minutes limit and scored 33.

Smith started Chicago's games through Nov. 18 at 21 to 32 minutes even after Nic Claxton returned in a bench role. The show said Claxton's return has not hurt Smith and that the Chicago staff seems to trust him. Smith did not play on Nov. 20, and Claxton started that game.

Smith has started every Bulls game in the box scores since early November and hit six threes for 26 points on November 22. The show said he has been very good and that it does not expect his play to stop.

Jalen Smith played 34 minutes on 11/22 before fouling out, and Nic Claxton missed that game with an illness, so there was no center split to deal with. The show said Smith has played at a third-round fantasy level in what it expects to be a fill-in role.

Jalen Smith has started each game he has played for Chicago in this stretch, but he has been in and out of the lineup. He played 34 minutes on Nov. 22 and scored 26 points. The show said he has been very good when available and that his health is the main thing to check.
Jalen Smith started and played 25 minutes while Nic Claxton played 23 off the bench, so the two split the center minutes almost evenly. The show said Smith is the better play if that split continues.

Jalen Suggs played 30 minutes in his third straight start on 11/20, which follows 31 minutes in his previous game. The show called the minutes encouraging and said his return has not cut into Anthony Black's role so far.

Jalen Suggs played only 22 minutes on Nov. 22 because of foul trouble after 30 and 31 minutes in his previous two games. The show does not expect Orlando to give his starting role to Anthony Black because Suggs is too important defensively.
Jalen Suggs was limited to 22 minutes by foul trouble and shot poorly on a usage rate the show put at 27 percent. The show said he should be better than this and is not a drop.

Jalen Suggs has been back in Orlando's starting lineup since 11/16, and he reached 31 minutes in his third game back on 11/18. The show said he has shot poorly in each of his last two games but still has a high ceiling at $5,500.

The show said Suggs does not have the same minutes ceiling as Anthony Black, which matters more on a three-game slate, so it ranked Orlando's guards Black first, Desmond Bane second and Suggs third. The show also said Orlando's defense has looked different with Suggs in the lineup versus out of it.
He is ruled out tonight (left ankle surgery). Mitchell had 18 points, six rebounds, four assists and three steals in 28 minutes when Williams and Cason Wallace got hurt Sunday.
Jamal Murray dealt with foul trouble Monday and was hounded all night by Dillon Brooks, though he still scored 28 in 35 minutes.
Murray played 45 minutes on Sunday, Nov. 22, because the game went to overtime, up from 36 to 38 in his previous games, and he scored eight of Denver's overtime points.
Jamal Murray scored 45 points with six threes, three steals and two blocks in 45 minutes in an overtime win over Chicago. The show said he is the fifth-ranked fantasy player over the last two weeks.

Murray played 45 minutes on Sunday, which the show said was an overtime game, after 36, 38 and 35 minutes in the three games before it. The show said he is shooting extremely well with a 67% true shooting rate, while his assist rate has dipped to about 25% as he gets more open shots playing off Jokic.

Murray scored 45 points for 73.75 DraftKings points in 45 minutes on Nov. 22. The show said Dallas is not capable of slowing him down and named him its top get-different play at $8,800, while noting he needs 50 or more points to pay off.

Jamal Shead has come off the bench in the Raptors' games since November 11, including the two games RJ Barrett has missed. The show said he is an assist and steal specialist worth rostering while Barrett is out. His bench minutes have not grown yet, since he played 24 minutes on November 18 and only 15 minutes on November 20.
The show said Jamal Shead should get a few extra minutes with RJ Barrett out for a couple of weeks. It called dropping him a mistake now that the Toronto injuries have popped up.
Jamal Shead played 26 minutes off the bench on 11/23. The show said he is a streamer for assists only.

The show said James Harden told the media he did not play much in the offseason and is playing his way into game shape. It said his assists, free throws and steals have all improved over his last two games, and he had 20 points, 8 assists and 3 steals in 35 minutes on November 13.

The show said James Harden is clearly the second option behind Donovan Mitchell, but the two have started to produce well in the same games with Evan Mobley out. Mobley has not played since 11/11, and in the three games since then Mitchell scored 41.5, 55.5 and 45 DraftKings points while Harden scored 47.5, 31 and 37.

Harden had another poor shooting night on Wednesday and finished with 14 points and nine assists. The show said it does not think he bounces back to his old level and believes this may just be who he is now.

Harden scored 51 points on November 20. The show said reports describe him as playing his way into shape, his field goal percentage has climbed to about 41 percent, and it expects him to keep improving.

James Harden scored 51 points in 40 minutes on November 20 with Evan Mobley out. The show said Mobley is still out for Monday, so ceiling games remain possible for Harden against Chicago, which is on the second night of a back-to-back.

James Wiseman played 25 minutes as the backup center on 11/21 with Andre Drummond moving into the starting lineup for Karl-Anthony Towns. He had five points, six rebounds and three blocks after playing only 3 minutes on 11/15. The show said he would be interesting in deeper leagues if Drummond ever got hurt.

Toronto played without Scottie Barnes and Kawhi Leonard against Boston. The show said Jamison Battle turned the ball over on an inbound with Toronto down three and 15 seconds left; he played 25 minutes and scored 12 points.

Jamison Battle started and played 33 minutes with RJ Barrett out, after playing only eight and seven minutes in his previous two games. The show said that is what happens when Barrett sits, and it expects most Raptors back soon.

Jamison Battle played 20 minutes off the bench on 11/20 after he started and played 33 minutes on 11/18. The show said he has a little more to do with RJ Barrett out, but his minutes could drop once Collin Murray-Boyles returns.
Jarace Walker was taken out of Indiana's rotation along with Jay Huff, and both played only one minute in garbage time. Jalen Slawson took over those minutes.
Jared McCain was listed as a streaming option because Cason Wallace and Jalen Williams and Chet Holmgren are out, which opens up minutes for him. McCain played 33 minutes in his last game on 11/18.
He is ruled out tonight (right mcl tear).

The show said Jaren Jackson Jr. is probably out at least another month; he has not played since October 26. The show said he will come back to a crowded Utah offense, with Darryn Peterson playing much better and Keyonte George taking a lot of shots.
He is questionable Friday against Philadelphia with a knee issue after playing only seven minutes Wednesday, and Peyton Watson is questionable with hamstring soreness.
He missed Friday with his knee injury, and Peyton Watson started and played 28 minutes, but the show said Watson will probably sit Saturday against New York.

He is questionable at Charlotte after missing the last two games, and Sam Merrill and Jaylon Tyson are already out. Meleek Thomas started Saturday with Merrill out and is a value play if he starts again.
Jarrett Allen played 31 minutes on 11/20 with Evan Mobley out with a toe sprain. The show said Allen has been a bit underwhelming without Mobley and that his upside is limited.

Javon Small has moved into a much bigger bench role, playing 30 and 29 minutes in the last two games after 15-minute nights on 11/11 and 11/13. The show said he is eating into Cam Spencer's usage with the ball in his hands a lot and called him a strong points-per-minute value. The show also said Spencer is still too cheap at $5.6K and that both can be played together.

Small has played a bigger bench role while Ty Jerome sits with a hip problem, logging 30 and 29 minutes on 11/14 and 11/16. The show said he only matters as long as Jerome is out and has little use once Jerome returns. On 11/18, with Jerome still out, Small played 21 minutes and scored 2 points.

Javon Small played 25 minutes off the bench on November 19 with Ty Jerome out. The show said he is on a two-way contract in a crowded backcourt, so Memphis tends to use him when guards are injured. He was ruled out on November 21 for personal reasons.

Javon Small scored 17.8 of his 32.2 DraftKings points in garbage time of a 28-point win against GSW on Thursday, when the lead was 20 or more late. His line is bigger than his normal role; expect less in a close game.
Javonte Green played 23 minutes on 11/17 because Detroit only had nine players available. The show said he is playable only if Detroit is missing the same players again.

Green started and played 35 minutes on 11/18 because Cade Cunningham, Duncan Robinson and Ronald Holland II were all out. The show said it does not expect him to start on 11/20 if Cunningham returns, and it thinks his price is now too high for that role.

The show said Green is a better all-around player than Josh Green but sits in a bench role of about 20 minutes. He started and played 35 minutes on November 18 while Ronald Holland II was out, then played 23 minutes off the bench on November 20.

Hayes is back from his absence and retook the Jazz starting center job on 11/20, playing 28 minutes. The show said Jusuf Nurkic's return would complicate the role again later, but Hayes is the starter for now.

Jaxson Hayes played only 12 minutes on 11/22 before hurting his left knee, and he was ruled out on 11/23 with a left knee strain. The show said it is the same knee that kept him out for several games earlier, and he did miss games between 11/13 and 11/18. No return date was given.

Hayes left Sunday's loss to Dallas with a knee injury and is questionable at the Lakers, leaving Mo Bamba as Utah's next center with Jusuf Nurkic and Jaren Jackson Jr. out. Svi Mykhailiuk has played 28 to 34 bench minutes in four straight games.
Jaylen Brown faces Boston, his former team, for the first time on Nov. 10. He has scored 20 or more points in each of Philadelphia's last four games while playing 33 to 37 minutes.

Jaylen Brown is out at Orlando with a left hamstring strain he felt late Monday. Tyrese Maxey and Joel Embiid take on more of the offense, and Dean Wade, Anfernee Simons and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope pick up the wing minutes.
He is ruled out tonight (left hamstring strain).

Jaylen Brown returned from a two-game absence with a hamstring injury on Monday and went straight back into the starting lineup for 29 minutes. Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, who had started while Brown was out, went back to the bench and played 17 minutes.
Brown is probable against Portland after missing every game since November 16 with a hamstring strain, which should send Kentavious Caldwell-Pope back to the bench.
Jaylon Tyson started for the second straight game and played 34 minutes on 11/14 while Cleveland rested its regulars. The show called his game solid and said Cavaliers rest days are worth monitoring.
The show expects Jaylon Tyson to be available soon and would add him now over Tyrese Proctor. The show said Tyson and Sam Merrill returning would take about 50 minutes away from Proctor and others.
Jaylon Tyson played only 12 minutes on 11/23 with Evan Mobley out, after the show expected him to get about 25. The show said his upside is not high enough to care.
Kent started Tuesday at Minnesota with Deni Avdija out and played 27 minutes, alongside Sidy Cissoko in the starting group.
Jayson Kent started the last two games in place of Deni Avdija, who has a left foot injury, but he played only 17 minutes on Thursday, Nov. 19.
He rested Wednesday for his first missed game of the season, and Payton Pritchard missed the fourth quarter with a right eye abrasion. Sam Hauser started and Derrick White scored 24 in 36 minutes.

Jayson Tatum played both games of Boston's 11/10-11/11 back-to-back, and he played 30 minutes on 11/15 before the 11/16 game against Orlando. The show said Tatum is a strong spend-up if he plays the back-to-back because Orlando plays more one-on-one coverage this year.
He is questionable tonight at SAC.

Tatum rested Saturday in Boston's one-point loss at Sacramento and was expected back Sunday at Golden State, while Derrick White (shoulder) could also return. Boston has not filed today's report, and Payton Pritchard started Saturday in their place.

The show said losing Jaylen Brown has let Tatum run Boston's offense the way he wants, and it cited a 33% usage rate and a 34% assist rate. He has played 38, 37 and 36 minutes in his last three games, and the show called him a little underpriced at $9,700 on the three-game slate.

Jerami Grant scored 22 points off the bench Friday but left with 7:36 to play after a collision with Herbert Jones. Memphis has not posted tonight's report for Brooklyn yet. Quinten Post (concussion protocol) and Zach Edey (ankle) also missed Friday.

Jerami Grant has settled into a steady bench role for Memphis, playing 20 to 26 minutes in recent games including 23 minutes on 11/16. The show said Memphis is comfortable using him in that role and called him the main sub-$5K value.

Grant left Thursday's win early with a left calf injury after five minutes, with Ty Jerome and Zach Edey already out. Jahmai Mashack (26 minutes) and Olivier-Maxence Prosper (24) picked up the extra time; Memphis plays Saturday at Minnesota.

Jerami Grant is out with a left calf strain after leaving Thursday's game, joining Cameron Boozer, Javon Small, Scotty Pippen Jr. and GG Jackson on the sideline. Jaylen Wells, Taylor Hendricks and Cedric Coward are the healthy forwards left, and Ty Jerome is probable.
The show said Jerami Grant is hurt, which takes another forward out of the Memphis rotation while Cameron Boozer is out. Grant did not play on 11/21 or 11/23 after playing only 5 minutes on 11/19.

Jeremiah Fears posted his first career triple-double with 19 points, 10 rebounds and 10 assists against Golden State on 11/16. He has been running the offense with Dejounte Murray out, and the show preferred him over others in the $7,000 range.
Jeremiah Fears played 38 minutes on Friday, Nov. 20, up from about 31 in his previous five games, and he stayed on the floor through the close finish at Oklahoma City.

Jeremiah Fears scored 29 points in 34 minutes on 11/21 with Zion Williamson, Trey Murphy III and Dejounte Murray all out. He has started and played 29 to 38 minutes in each of his last six games. The show said his arrow is pointing firmly up.
Jeremiah Fears played 40 minutes and ran the offense with 11 assists on Monday, but he missed 14 of 17 shots two nights after scoring 29 at San Antonio.
Jericho Sims started for Milwaukee on November 15 but played only 11 minutes, while Kel'el Ware played 25 minutes off the bench. The show did not see any value in the Sims start.

Jericho Sims started at center for Milwaukee in a game where Myles Turner had foul trouble and played 21 minutes. The show said the start was a surprise in a Taylor Jenkins rotation where everybody plays.
Jericho Sims started Milwaukee's previous two games but came off the bench and played only 10 minutes on November 19. The show said none of the Bucks' starting choices make sense.
Jimmy Butler is still out while he recovers from right ACL surgery, and he is ruled out for Monday, November 16.
Joan Beringer played 19 minutes behind Rudy Gobert on 11/23. The show said it is confident he will not take over Gobert's starting job this season.
Beringer has played between 13 and 26 minutes off the bench behind Rudy Gobert. The show said his role would grow only if Minnesota cuts Gobert's minutes or Gobert gets hurt.
Jock Landale was held out on Friday, Nov. 20, with a back issue, leaving Zuby Ejiofor as the backup center.

Joel Embiid and LeBron James are both questionable tonight against Toronto for injury management. Dean Wade has started every game this season that either one missed, and Tyrese Maxey gains usage if both sit.
He is ruled out tonight. Embiid sits the second night of back-to-backs, and Edgecombe does more when stars are out.

Joel Embiid scored 37 points in 32 minutes against Brooklyn on 11/16. The show said his usage is high no matter who plays, and removing Jaylen Brown's roughly 30% usage share makes him more interesting while Brown is out. The show said his minutes are the main concern because they bounce around.

Joel Embiid sat Sunday's front end of the back-to-back, when Jabari Walker started and Dean Wade played 35 minutes. LeBron James played 33 minutes Sunday. Philadelphia had not posted its report for Brooklyn on Monday morning.
Joel Embiid did not play Monday against Portland because of an illness.

Joel Embiid has scored 50 or more DraftKings points in three straight games while taking 10 or more free throws in each one, including 26 points, 17 rebounds and nine assists in 34 minutes on November 21. The show said his foot is fine and that his trips to the line give him a high floor against Portland.

Collins is starting with Jalen Duren out, but Paul Reed out-minuted him off the bench on 11/20 (28 minutes to 20), and Reed did it again on 11/22 (26 to 22). The show said Collins is not a lock to start and becomes very hard to use once Duren returns.

John Collins is starting at center for Detroit with Jalen Duren out, but he played only 22 minutes on 11/22 because he shares the job with Paul Reed. The show said Collins is a low-usage player whose recent value comes from hot shooting, and it called him a streamer until Duren returns in about a week.

With Jalen Duren out, Collins started and played 22 minutes while Paul Reed played 26 off the bench, which was a little closer than the 20-to-28 split two days earlier. The show said the center minutes tipped slightly back toward Collins, but it still sees Reed as the better of the two because his stat set supports it.
John Collins was listed as a high-end streamer with Jalen Duren out. Collins played 22 minutes in his last game on 11/22.

Jonathan Kuminga left Monday's win over Portland with a right shoulder injury, and Minnesota had not posted its injury report Tuesday morning. Terrence Shannon Jr. played 35 minutes off the bench Monday with Anthony Edwards and Jaylen Clark out and scored a career-high 34.

Jonathan Kuminga played 35 minutes as a starter and went 7 of 7 from the free throw line. The show said one good free throw night does not change that he has been a poor free throw shooter this season. The show credited his higher steals and blocks partly to getting 30-plus minutes that Golden State never gave him.
Kuminga returned Thursday from a two-game absence with a bruised right shoulder and played 35 minutes with no sign of a limit, starting for Minnesota against New York.
He is questionable tonight vs NYK.
Jonathan Kuminga was listed as a top-100 season-long pickup with Anthony Edwards out but only for teams that punt free-throw percentage. Kuminga played 37 minutes in his last game on 11/21.

Jonathan Kuminga played 26 minutes in a 26-point win against BKN on Monday, 6 under his average over his previous 5 games, and sat most of the 9 minutes of garbage time. His 29.2 DraftKings points likely undersell his normal role.

Jordan Goodwin has been part of the Phoenix bench rotation, playing 24, 31 and 20 minutes over his last three games. He contributes across several categories, with 14 points, seven rebounds and six assists in his 31-minute game on 11/15. The show said he is similar to Kenrich Williams as a low-volume, multi-category player, but that his shooting percentage has been a drag over the past week.

Goodwin has been a regular part of the Phoenix bench, playing between 17 and 31 minutes in each of his last four games without a start. The show said he has been scoring off the bench and could become a viable streamer if he strings together a few more good games.

Jordan Goodwin played 28 minutes off the bench on 11/20 with nine rebounds, four assists and two steals, while Collin Gillespie also played 27 bench minutes. The show said Phoenix is spreading minutes so widely that the bench plays as much as the starters, and that one guard injury would make Goodwin or Gillespie an every-game play.
Jordan Hawkins got 18 minutes off the bench on Monday when Chicago spread out playing time the night after an overtime loss, and the Bulls' bench scored 63 points.
With Dylan Harper out one to three weeks, McLaughlin moved into the Spurs' rotation Thursday and played 11 minutes in a close game, and San Antonio outscored the Clippers by 16 with him on the floor.
The show said Miller is out for about six months.

With Dejounte Murray out since 11/11 (the injury report lists a left ankle sprain), Poole played 30 to 31 minutes off the bench on 11/16 and 11/18 and scored in double figures in five straight games. Trey Murphy III returned on 11/20 and played 29 minutes, and that night Poole fell to 13 minutes and 6 points. The show taped before that game and called Poole a strong two-day streamer.

Jordan Poole played 30 minutes on November 18 while Trey Murphy III was out, but he dropped to 13 minutes on November 20 when Murphy returned. The show had warned that Murphy's return would cut into Poole's role, so Poole's value depends on Murphy's status.

Poole has played 30 or more minutes off the bench in three of his last four games, including 25 points in 31 minutes on Nov. 21. The show said his revival is boosted by the absences of Dejounte Murray and Trey Murphy III but that the new coaching staff may also have grown to like him.

Poole played 31 minutes off the bench on Saturday with Zion Williamson (thigh), Trey Murphy III (knee) and Bennedict Mathurin (plantar fasciitis) all out, and he and Jeremiah Fears carried the scoring.
Poole has played 31 and 27 minutes off the bench and scored 25 and 28 points in his last two games after only 13 minutes on 11/20. Dan Besbris asked whether he is worth an add while he is this hot.
Jordan Poole came off the bench for 27 minutes on Monday and made his first nine shots, but all of his scoring came in the first three quarters and he was not a factor late or in overtime.
Walsh started but played only four minutes and was moved out of the lineup to begin the second half. The show did not understand why Boston keeps starting him.
Alvarado played 22 minutes off the bench on Sunday, Nov. 22, up from 7 to 15 in his previous three games, with Deuce McBride held out.
Dix played 32 minutes off the bench on Sunday, Nov. 22, and closed the game, with Oklahoma City down to nine available players and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander out.

Josh Giddey had 57 DraftKings points in 39 minutes on 11/13, but he dropped to 26 minutes and 28 points on 11/14 against Minnesota's strong defense. The show still liked his ceiling and expected him to be low-owned on 11/16.

Josh Giddey played only 24 minutes on 11/16 with six turnovers and four points, and Tre Jones took on more of the work. The show said Chicago will not play guys who are playing badly, which puts Giddey's minutes at risk when he struggles.

The show said Chicago has played better team basketball since rookie Caleb Wilson went out, with wins in three of four games. Giddey had 15 points, 10 rebounds and 14 assists on November 13 and 18 points, 14 rebounds and 9 assists on November 18 during that stretch, with two quieter games in between.

The show said Josh Giddey is running only a 20% usage rate with 52% true shooting this season, and that having Norman Powell and Caleb Wilson in the lineup hurt both Giddey and Matas Buzelis. Caleb Wilson was ruled out again for 11/20 and has not played since 11/11, so the show said one of those usage threats is gone.

Giddey played 41 minutes in an overtime game with Norman Powell out and posted 23 points, 14 rebounds and 22 assists on 17 shots, one game after a two-point night. The show said it will almost certainly be his best game of the season, because the Bulls shot far above their level and they have been the worst three-point shooting team in the league. He fell back to 22 minutes and four points on November 23.

Giddey played only 22 minutes on Monday, the night after his 22-assist overtime game against Denver, because the Bulls spread out playing time on the back-to-back. Tre Jones played 27 minutes off the bench.
Josh Green got the start for Utah and played 28 minutes, his most since November 10. The show said fantasy players can ignore it.
Green has started Utah's last two games and played 28 and 29 minutes. The show said it is confident he keeps starting, but warned he gives little production outside defensive stats.
Josh Green is still in Utah's starting lineup, but he scored zero points in 23 minutes. The show mocked his empty production and treated him as a starter with no fantasy value.
He is questionable tonight vs CLE.

Josh Hart has scored zero points in each of his last two games, going 0-for-9 from the field combined, and he averaged 4.1 points over his last seven games in the box scores. He is still starting and played 23 and 26 minutes in those two games. The show said his production has been bad for about three weeks and that New York is leaning more on Landry Shamet.

The show said Josh Hart has been benched late in recent games, which makes his minutes a risk even though he keeps starting. Hart has played only 23 to 26 minutes in each of his last three games. The show said Landry Shamet and Miles McBride are the players who benefit when Hart or Mikal Bridges get benched, and it expects Shamet to play 25 to 30 minutes most nights.

Hart is still starting but scored zero points on 11/13 and 11/15 and five on 11/17. The show said his usage rate has been under 10 percent in each of his last three games. The show believes he is playing through an injury that may only be fixed by surgery, which he likely wants to avoid.

Hart is still starting, but Landry Shamet has played 24 to 30 minutes off the bench in recent games. Hart scored 0 points on both 11/13 and 11/15 before he had 11 points with three threes in 28 minutes on 11/19. The show said Shamet is the hot hand right now, but it expects Hart to work his way back.

The show said Josh Hart and Mikal Bridges have both been afterthoughts in the Knicks offense at about seven shots a game. Hart took nine shots on Thursday, while Bridges took seven. The show prefers Hart because his rebounds and defensive stats have been better.

The show said the Knicks' wings have been vocal that this year's offense is hard on them because it is so centered on Jalen Brunson, and Hart is getting fewer and worse looks, with far fewer slashing twos. The show said Karl-Anthony Towns's heavy rebounding has cut into Hart's boards and Landry Shamet has been firing threes off the bench. Hart is still playing near 30 minutes, and the show expects his shooting to improve.

Josh Hart scored zero points on 11/21 despite playing 35 minutes, his third scoreless game in his last five. He still had eight rebounds, six assists and two steals. The show said he is in a deep shooting slump tied to a finger issue but expects him to come around because the minutes and impact are there.

Hart posted a triple-double in 39 minutes on November 22 after a long slump that included three scoreless games in his previous six. The show said his usage, including assists, is down about three and a half percent, so it does not expect him to return to his old level even if his shooting improves.

Josh Okogie and Josh Green have traded the open starting spot in Utah, with Okogie starting on November 13 and Green on November 15. The show expects one of them to start again on Tuesday. Okogie still played 27 minutes off the bench on November 15.
Josh Okogie scored all nine of his points in the fourth quarter Tuesday as part of the bench group that pulled away from the Clippers; he played 10 of the quarter's 12 minutes.

Jrue Holiday has played 31 minutes off the bench in each of the last two games with Deni Avdija out, and he scored 22 points with seven assists and four steals on Thursday. The show said Holiday moves into a bigger fantasy tier while Avdija is sidelined.

Jrue Holiday kept a big bench role with Deni Avdija back in the lineup, playing 31 minutes with 13 points, 9 rebounds and 7 assists. He has now played 25 to 31 minutes off the bench in six straight games, and the show said his production holding up with Avdija back is a good sign.
Jrue Holiday continues to come off the bench for Portland and played 28 minutes on 11/23. The show said he has been playing well in that sixth-man role.

Julian Champagnie started and played 29 minutes with Dylan Harper out, and he took 14 shots. The show said Champagnie is probably a play everywhere while Harper is sidelined and that he brings more threes than Devin Vassell. The show contrasted this with De'Aaron Fox's earlier absence, which did not free up enough usage to lift either player.

Julian Champagnie moved into the starting lineup on November 19 and November 21 with Dylan Harper out, after coming off the bench on November 17. He played 29 and 25 minutes in those starts, and the show asked whether he can stay useful on a nightly basis in this role.

Dan Besbris said Champagnie is a good play while Dylan Harper is out, and even better when more Spurs sit. With Wembanyama, Fox and Harper all out on 11/23, Champagnie started and played 30 minutes for 39.25 DK points.
