The Kings signed Mason Plumlee. The show cited Kings reporter James Ham saying the signing was not because of an injury to Domantas Sabonis or a significant injury to Precious Achiuwa. The show also said the Kings are pursuing Gabe Vincent for their other open roster spot.

With Caleb Wilson out, Matas Buzelis scored 23 and 25 points in his November 16 and 18 games while playing about 30 minutes each night. The show said the Bulls look better since the rookie's usage left the lineup.
Matas Buzelis played only 25 minutes on 11/20 after he played 29 to 31 minutes in each of his previous five games. The show said early foul trouble kept him from getting into a rhythm.
The show said Matas Buzelis is bouncing back and that the Bulls are playing better without Caleb Wilson, whose offense had been built on giving him the ball. Wilson has not played since November 11.

Matas Buzelis played 38 minutes and has been much better over the last two weeks. The show said Caleb Wilson being out is a big reason for the bump, and Wilson's return is a risk for the second half of the season.
Buzelis was also benched in the fourth quarter on Friday, Nov. 20, but played 38 minutes and closed Sunday's overtime game with Norman Powell and Caleb Wilson out.

The show said Buzelis has put up several 30-plus DraftKings games since Chicago players started going down with injuries. He played 38 minutes on 11/22 and scored 37.25 DraftKings points, and he had 44.75 on 11/18. The show listed him as a GPP pivot at $6,200.
Matas Buzelis started and played 27 minutes on Monday, but all 15 of his points came in the first half as Chicago spread out minutes the night after an overtime game.

Thybulle is a starter for the Lakers and has posted at least three steals in six straight games through 11/17. He also had at least one block and at least two threes in each of his last four games through that date. The show said his value comes almost entirely from steals, blocks and threes because he scores little.

Matisse Thybulle has recorded at least three steals in seven straight games, including four on Nov. 18, while starting for the Lakers. The show said his defense keeps him in the lineup whether or not Austin Reaves plays, even though he scores very little.

Thybulle has started every Lakers game and has not played fewer than 21 minutes since November 4. The show said his value comes from elite steals and blocks rather than scoring, and he had at least three steals in three of his last four games.

Thybulle has started every Lakers game in this stretch at 21 to 31 minutes as a defensive specialist beside Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves. The show said his role and minutes look safe because JJ Redick wants defenders around his two stars, and he has recorded three or more steals in seven of his last eight games.

Matisse Thybulle is starting for the Lakers and has played 27 minutes in each of his last two games. The show said he has no pressure to score next to Luka Doncic, Austin Reaves, Quentin Grimes and Walker Kessler, so he can focus on defense and threes. He has posted at least two combined steals and blocks in every game in this stretch.
Matisse Thybulle played 27 minutes on 11/23 with Austin Reaves out. The show said he will probably lose some minutes when Reaves returns.
Max Christie is questionable at Cleveland with a left ankle sprain, and Dereck Lively II remains out. Naji Marshall and Zaccharie Risacher take the extra wing minutes if Christie sits.
Christie returned Wednesday from a two-game absence with a left ankle sprain and was eased back in at eight minutes.

Max Christie played 24 minutes off the bench on 11/21 after playing only 8 minutes on 11/18. He scored 13 points with three threes and three steals. The show said it would not be surprised if he moves back into the starting lineup but called him mainly a points-and-threes player.

Max Strus replaced Kris Dunn as the starting shooting guard and played 32 minutes after not topping 25 minutes in any earlier game this season. The show said the Clippers are signaling they want to see this team with Strus as the last starter, and it noted his usage rate in this game was higher than in any of his Cleveland seasons. He scored 18 points with five threes even though he picked up five fouls.

The show said Strus now sits right behind Darius Garland and Rui Hachimura in the Clippers' pecking order, since the roster has no high-usage star like Donovan Mitchell ahead of him. The show added that if Garland ever takes a day off, Strus could become the lead scorer because Kris Dunn would run the point but does not score. The show warned that a return by Brandon Ingram, who has not played this season, would cut into the usage for every Clipper other than Garland.

Strus moved into the Clippers' starting lineup on 11/19 and played 32 minutes with five threes, then started again on 11/21 and played 29 minutes but shot poorly. The show said the role and minutes held, so the 11/21 dip was shooting variance, but it wants to see his role after Brandon Ingram returns.
Strus moved to the bench on 11/23 when Brandon Ingram returned and started, and he scored only 12.5 DK points in 26 minutes. Dan Besbris said Strus can be dropped.
Maxime Raynaud remained out on 11/23. The show said Sacramento has given no clear timeline and guessed he is still about a week away.

Meleek Thomas played 30 minutes off the bench with Evan Mobley and Jaylon Tyson both out. The show said Thomas could slide into the starting five if Peyton Watson also misses time, and it sees him as a points, threes and steals contributor.

The show named Thomas, along with Tyrese Proctor, as the likely fill-ins for the starting spots left open by Evan Mobley and Peyton Watson. He started and played 34 minutes on 11/14 when the regular starters rested, but he came off the bench for 22 minutes on 11/18 once Donovan Mitchell, James Harden and Jarrett Allen were back.

Meleek Thomas came off the bench for 22 minutes on Wednesday because Mario Hezonja, not Thomas, took the second open starting spot. The show said Thomas's recent production relied on unsustainable shooting and steals and that he is a streamer without 28 or more minutes.

Meleek Thomas is a steady bench scorer for the Cavaliers, playing about 20 to 30 minutes a night, and he started on November 14 when the Cavs rested players. The show said Thomas has forced his way into the rotation even when everyone is healthy and is one injury away from a bigger role. Tyrese Proctor has held the starting spot since November 14 while Thomas has come off the bench.
Peavy started and played 31 minutes on Sunday, Nov. 22, after playing 9 off the bench in his previous game, as Oklahoma City dressed only nine players with Shai Gilgeous-Alexander out.
Michael Porter Jr. has picked up shooting guard eligibility on DraftKings after Brooklyn moved Danny Wolf out of the starting lineup. The show said it would definitely play him on Wednesday.

Michael Porter Jr. played 27 minutes in a 30-point loss against CHI on Wednesday, 7 under his average over his previous 5 games, and sat most of the 12 minutes of garbage time. His 12.2 DraftKings points likely undersell his normal role.
The show said Porter is now shooting guard eligible on DraftKings. It also called tonight's game against Chicago a good matchup and expects Brooklyn-Chicago stacks to come up often.

Mikal Bridges is still starting, but the show said he has been on a short leash and was pulled about five minutes into a recent game. His minutes have swung from 17 in two games last week to 29 and 32 in his last two, including 18 points on November 13. The show said the scoring has been poor while the steals have come back.

The show said Mikal Bridges is getting better and his minutes are up, with 31 minutes on November 19 after 30 and 32 in two of his previous three games. His scoring is weak, so his value comes from defensive stats like his two steals and a block.
Mikal Bridges played 31 minutes despite scoring 8 points on 25 percent shooting. The show said it would drop him.
Conley played 18 minutes off the bench on Saturday with Jayson Tatum and Derrick White out and was in Boston's closing lineup.

Mike Conley re-entered Boston's rotation on Nov. 21 after not playing since Nov. 8. He played 18 minutes with Jayson Tatum and Derrick White out and scored 19 points, then still played 16 minutes on Nov. 22 when both returned. The show said some of Payton Pritchard's guard minutes are now going to Conley.
He is questionable tonight at MEM.

Brown has played 18 to 27 minutes off the bench in recent games and scored 18 points in 24 minutes on 11/20. The show listed him as an option for week six because the Nets play four games and Nolan Traore is likely out all week.
Brown moved into Brooklyn's starting lineup on 11/23 with Nolan Traore out with a hamstring strain, and he played 29 minutes for 34.75 DK points. Dan Besbris called him an add for guard-needy builds.
Mikel Brown Jr. has played 24 to 27 minutes off the bench in his last two games. The show said the rookie's shooting has been very poor so far, but it expects that to improve as he finds his form.
Phoenix played on Nov. 9, so the Nov. 10 game is the second night of a back-to-back for Miles Bridges and the Suns. Bridges played only 26 minutes with 17.25 DraftKings points on Nov. 9.

Bridges is still starting at power forward for Phoenix, but his minutes have dropped from 31 in early November to between 18 and 26 over his last four games. The show called it a cold spell and said it expects him to bounce back because the Suns need his scoring and playmaking.

The show said Phoenix is aggressively cutting starters' minutes when they play poorly and sending bench players in, which held Miles Bridges to 29 minutes, Jalen Green to 27 and Dillon Brooks to 27. In the previous game against the Lakers, the Suns benched most of the starters during a bench-led comeback.
The show said Miles McBride's minutes are too unpredictable to trust. He has gone from 25 and 27 minutes to 22 and then 14 minutes on November 15.

The show called Miles McBride one of the most unpredictable minutes players in the league after he played only eight minutes. He has played 14, 9 and 8 minutes in his last three games after logging 22 to 27 minutes earlier in November.
McBride was held out on Sunday, Nov. 22, with left adductor tightness, his first missed game of the season.

The show said Mitchell Robinson is out Tuesday with an illness, and he also did not play on Nov. 21 or Nov. 22. The show expects Neemias Queta to play about 29 minutes and Luka Garza 15 to 16 minutes without him.
He is ruled out tonight (illness). Queta would take the starting center minutes and Garza the backup minutes.

With Jusuf Nurkic and Jaxson Hayes out again, Mo Bamba should keep the starting center job after playing 36 minutes Sunday. Keyonte George sprained his right ankle Sunday but is not on Utah's injury report.

Bamba started and played 36 and 31 minutes on 11/15 and 11/17 while Jaxson Hayes was out. Hayes returned to the starting lineup on 11/20, and Bamba dropped to 20 bench minutes. The show also said Jusuf Nurkic is returning fairly soon, which would push Bamba down further.

Bamba started and played 36 and 31 minutes on Nov. 15 and Nov. 17 while Jaxson Hayes was out, but he went back to a 20-minute bench role on Nov. 20 when Hayes started. The show said Bamba's value has ended now that Hayes is healthy.

Mo Bamba is the Utah starter at center when Jaxson Hayes is out, and he started again on 11/23 with Hayes out with a knee strain. When Bamba started earlier this month he played 36 minutes on 11/15 and 31 minutes on 11/17. The show called him a top-50-level fill-in whenever he starts.
Bamba played 23 minutes off the bench on Sunday, Nov. 22, after Jaxson Hayes left with a knee injury, with Utah already missing Jusuf Nurkic and Jaren Jackson Jr. up front.
Dan Besbris called Bamba a must-play with Utah's other centers hurt. He started on 11/23 with Jaxson Hayes, Jusuf Nurkic and Jaren Jackson Jr. out and played 29 minutes.
He played a season-high 24 minutes off the bench Friday with 13 points and 17 rebounds, while starter Daniel Gafford played only 18 minutes for the second straight game.
Morez Johnson Jr. missed Dallas's game on November 9 after a poor game on November 8 in which he scored 4 points in 19 minutes. The show said fantasy players are fine to move on from him.
The show said Morez Johnson Jr. has looked bad and has blocked only two shots all season, which matches the box scores. The show thinks a preseason injury is still affecting him.

Rookie Morez Johnson Jr. is playing about 17 minutes per game for Dallas and averaging about 6 points and 4.7 rebounds in the box scores. The show said his finishing has been poor and he has not posted much defensive stat production, but he is doing his job as a defender in a limited role.

Morez Johnson Jr. had nine points, seven rebounds and two steals in 17 minutes off the bench on 11/21. He has played 15 to 26 minutes in his last four games. The show said the production is good but 17 minutes is not enough to make him a priority.

The show described Johnson as Daniel Gafford's backup center, so his main path to more minutes is Gafford getting into foul trouble. His minutes rose to 17 and 20 in the last two games while PJ Washington was out, and the show agreed that Washington had been soaking up some backup center minutes before that.
Morez Johnson Jr. has stayed in a reserve role of about 15 to 20 minutes and has added steals and rebounds in that time. The show said he would gain minutes if P.J. Washington misses Tuesday.

Morez Johnson Jr. has been Dallas's backup center and played 17 and 20 minutes in the last two games. The show said he has been a decent fantasy player but is very foul-prone, which is a bad fit against Nikola Jokic.
Moses Moody is out Thursday against Miami as he recovers from his knee injury; a return around January is the expectation.

Moses Moody, Gary Payton II and Brandin Williams did not play for Golden State against Houston. The show said those players will eventually return to help the guard rotation while Stephen Curry is hurt.
The show said Moussa Diabate is expected back for Charlotte on Nov 12 after missing games since Nov 4. The show said he should not be on a minutes limit and could post a double-double.
The show said Diabate was set up for a big game because Walker Kessler did not play for the Lakers on Nov. 17. He played 38 minutes in the overtime game and grabbed 16 rebounds.

Diabate has started every recent Hornets game and played 26 to 38 minutes, including 30 minutes on 11/20. The show said he is clearly the Charlotte center, and it said Ryan Kalkbrenner (14 to 18 minutes off the bench) is no threat to that role.
Myles Turner and Kyle Kuzma both rested on the second night of a back-to-back on November 19. The show said Turner is one of the only Bucks it trusts, mainly for blocks.

The show said Myles Turner has looked bad on offense this season, though he still gives about two blocks per game. He is averaging about 27 minutes per game in the box scores, and he has played 21 to 26 minutes in three of his last four games while Kel'el Ware's minutes have risen.
Myles Turner played only 26 minutes, and the show said he fouled out, though he still blocked 4 shots. The show called his shooting outrageously bad, since he scored 5 points on 8 shots.
The show said Myles Turner is not in danger of losing his starting center minutes to Kel'el Ware any time soon. He played 28 minutes on 11/23, and Ware played 23 off the bench.
Myles Turner fouled out at Toronto on Monday, which held him to 28 minutes even though he made five threes on six tries.
He was out for the Cavaliers' opener on Thursday.

Hyland played only 13 minutes on 11/16 while Terrence Shannon Jr. took 35 minutes off the bench, after Hyland had played 23 and 21 minutes in the two games before. The show said that if one more Minnesota player is ruled out, Hyland probably picks up a couple of extra minutes.

Naji Marshall scored 13.8 of his 25.2 DraftKings points in garbage time of a 22-point win against GSW on Wednesday, when the lead was 20 or more late. His line is bigger than his normal role; expect less in a close game.

The show called Naji Marshall the face of streaming this season because he plays 23 to 30 minutes and starts when Kyrie Irving or Cooper Flagg sits. He started on November 15 when Irving was out. Dallas plays Saturday and Sunday, so the show likes him for the weekend.

Naji Marshall played 25 minutes off the bench with P.J. Washington out with an illness. The show said Washington should be back soon and that Marshall is not worth holding while Cooper Flagg is healthy.

Naji Marshall's minutes have swung from 27 to 14 to 25 over his last three games, and the show called his season incredibly disappointing. The show said he is only a short-slate streaming option who gains if P.J. Washington stays out.

Ament started on 11/19 with Myles Turner and Kyle Kuzma both out and played 35 minutes, after 17 to 22 minutes in his previous five games. He scored 18 points with 9 rebounds. The show said the 19-year-old looks better than expected and could have regular 20-point nights about a month into a Milwaukee pivot to its young players.

The show said rookie Nate Ament is starting to get time on a thin Bucks wing group. He is averaging about 18.5 minutes per game in the box scores and started twice recently, including a 35-minute game on Nov 19, but he played only 14 minutes on Nov 21.

Naz Reid had a 35% usage rate but shot poorly, scoring 17 points on 20 shots. The show said his efficiency should improve as Coby White's minutes grow and once Kon Knueppel returns from his hamstring strain.

Reid played 42 minutes on 11/17 even with Coby White and Brandon Miller back in the lineup. The show said his role has not suffered from their returns and that bigs are the best way to attack Atlanta's strong perimeter defenders.

Reid has played 42 and 39 minutes in his last two games while Charlotte is missing Kon Knueppel, Dennis Schroder and Grayson Allen. The show said his minutes are there with little competition, and it preferred him to Brandon Miller among the 20 percent owned Hornets.
Neemias Queta rested on the second night of Boston's back-to-back while Paul George and Mitchell Robinson played. Luka Garza started in his place but played only 18 minutes.
Neemias Queta played 30 minutes as Boston's starting center with Mitchell Robinson out with an illness, posting 15 points and 7 rebounds. The show said Queta remains the Boston center to roster.
Neemias Queta played 30 minutes on the second night of a back-to-back but had a usage rate the show put at only 12 percent. The show still called him a must-roster player in category leagues.

Queta has started and played 30, 30, 27, 15 and 31 minutes in his last five games, and Mitchell Robinson is out again tonight with an illness. The show said Luka Garza does not bring much Boston wants, so Queta's starting minutes look secure, with foul trouble against Washington's bigs as the main risk. The show called him a core value at $5,100.
He is questionable at New York with a left hamstring strain, and Jalen Smith is probable with a finger sprain, so Chicago's center minutes are unsettled.

Nic Claxton came off the bench behind Jalen Smith and played 17 minutes with eight points. The show said that if he is still in this role in a week or two, it is not about his hamstring but about Smith being better.

The show said Nic Claxton is still on a slow ramp-up, and he has come off the bench for 16 to 22 minutes in each of his four games back. Jalen Smith remains the starter until Claxton's workload grows.

Nic Claxton has come off the bench for Chicago, playing 16 to 22 minutes, while Jalen Smith has started. The show said it has not been impressed with Claxton and that Smith has been playing well, though it called Smith an injury risk.

Nic Claxton played 22 minutes off the bench and has been rising in Chicago's center rotation. The show said Claxton should be at 22 to 24 minutes going forward, while starter Jalen Smith (21 minutes with foul trouble) has still been productive.

Claxton started and played 29 minutes on 11/20 while Jalen Smith was out sick. The show said that workload means there is no real minutes restriction left on Claxton, so the Bulls can use both centers fully. Claxton was then ruled out with an illness of his own on 11/22.

The show expects Nickeil Alexander-Walker to handle much of the ball with CJ McCollum and Kingston Flemings out. The show said it would rather target him than Dyson Daniels because he is the higher-usage player.
The show said Claxton's upside depends on Jalen Smith missing extended time or Claxton playing his way into a bigger role. He is currently behind Smith in the Bulls frontcourt.

Denver has leaned on Jokic heavily, with 42, 38, 39 and 38 minutes in his last four games, and the show projected him for about 37 minutes against Dallas. The show said Jokic and Jamal Murray are controlling Denver's fantasy production more than in past years because the rest of the roster is not producing.
Jovic posted a strong line but played only 19 minutes off the bench even with Giannis Antetokounmpo out. The show said to ignore the line because the minutes are still too limited to trust.
Topic left Wednesday's loss to Atlanta with left hip soreness after five minutes and did not return. He made his season debut Nov. 13 after offseason back surgery.

Vucevic returned to the rotation and played 23 minutes on November 20 after barely playing. The show said Orlando paired him with both Wendell Carter Jr. and Goga Bitadze and took Jamal Cain out of the rotation. The show said the defense was bad with those lineups, but the offense worked, so the team may keep trying it.
Nikola Vucevic played 23 minutes off the bench, his most in recent games after a run of 4 to 18 minutes. The show said it was his first good game of the year and that it can be ignored.

The show said Vucevic played alongside Wendell Carter Jr. last game and is no longer the main backup center, because Goga Bitadze is still taking the backup five minutes. It said Vucevic now seems to back up Franz Wagner instead, which gives him some assist upside, and he had 5 points, 3 rebounds and 3 assists in 17 minutes on Sunday.
Nikola Vucevic followed a big game with 5 points in 16 minutes off the bench. The show said the previous explosion was not a real trend.

Oklahoma City acquired Nique Clifford from Sacramento for two second-round picks, according to the show. Clifford had been out of the Kings' rotation, playing three to 11 minutes per game, and the show said Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Ajay Mitchell would still take most of the shots even if he wins a wing role.

The show said the Kings traded Nique Clifford to the Thunder, and it believes Murray's return made Sacramento comfortable with the move. Clifford had been buried for the Kings, playing between 2 and 17 minutes off the bench this season. His role in Oklahoma City is not yet known.
The show said Sacramento traded Nique Clifford to Oklahoma City for two second-round picks. He has come off the bench for the Thunder, playing 20 minutes on Nov. 10 and 16 minutes on Nov. 11.

Clifford played for Sacramento on Nov 6 and has appeared for Oklahoma City since Nov 10, all off the bench with 12 to 24 minutes. The show called him an upside add to see if he can carve out a role with the Thunder.

Noah Clowney started and played 35 minutes on November 14 while Michael Porter Jr. sat out, and he had 15 points, seven rebounds and three blocks. The show said that spike came from Porter resting and that it should be ignored.
Noah Clowney went back to the bench after starting the previous game for Michael Porter Jr., who returned to the lineup and played 40 minutes.

Traore moved back into the starting lineup next to Egor Demin on 11/16 and scored 23 points in 30 minutes. He has played at least 20 minutes in every game since late October and scored in double figures in every November game through 11/16. The show said he should be rostered everywhere.

The show said Nolan Traore was excellent in his last game and believes he is better than Egor Demin, but it worries that coach Jordi Fernandez cuts his minutes for stretches. Traore started and played 30 minutes on 11/16 after playing 20 minutes off the bench on 11/14.

Traore missed one game with calf soreness, came off the bench for 20 minutes on 11/14, then returned to Brooklyn's starting five on 11/16 (30 minutes) and started again on 11/18 (23 minutes). The show said nobody knows what the Nets' starting lineup will look like next week and that his minutes have been all over the map.

Nolan Traore is out with a right hamstring strain and was ruled out on Nov. 23. The show guessed it could be an 8 to 10 week absence if it is a grade three strain, but that timeline was speculation and not a reported diagnosis. He last played 18 minutes on Nov. 20.

The show said the Bulls have been so bad that Norman Powell is likely to be traded in January or February, probably into a bench scoring role on a playoff team. The show said four of his eight games have been blowouts that cut his minutes, and his box score minutes range from 22 to 37.

Powell returned from the injury report on 11/13 after missing games from 11/06 to 11/11, and he scored 33 and 24 points in 31 and 30 minutes as Chicago won both games. The show said he is in play at $6,100 on 11/16, especially if Cleveland is without Peyton Watson.

The show said Norman Powell's usage without Caleb Wilson has been ridiculous. He has scored 33, 24 and 27 points in the three games since Wilson went out, and on 11/16 he got to 27 points despite going 0-for-6 from three by getting to the line 11 times. The show called him its favorite play in his price range against Brooklyn.
Powell (hamstring) and Jalen Smith (illness) are questionable for Chicago against Denver in the slate's highest-total game, with Caleb Wilson already out.

Powell has a right hamstring strain and missed the November 22 and November 23 games. The show expected him to miss at least one more game and said he might return later in the week because the team calls the injury minor.
Obi Toppin has been held to 14 to 16 minutes in each of Indiana's last three games. The show said it does not understand why Indiana is not playing Toppin more.
Toppin played 26 minutes on November 20 after playing 14 to 17 minutes in the four games before that. The show said his bench minutes have swung back and forth and are hard to predict.
OG Anunoby is questionable with left calf tightness and Jordan Clarkson is out, which thins New York's rotation and puts more on Karl-Anthony Towns, Jalen Brunson and Landry Shamet.
Anunoby missed his second straight game on Sunday, Nov. 22, with tightness in his left calf. New York next plays Wednesday against Cleveland.

Prosper played 24 minutes off the bench Thursday with Ty Jerome and Zach Edey out and Jerami Grant leaving early with a calf injury. If Grant misses time, the forward minutes behind the starters are open.
Onyeka Okongwu played 36 minutes and had 16 points, 11 rebounds and three threes. The show said he had been stuck around 30 minutes, so the bigger minutes were a good sign.
Okongwu scored 28 points with five threes and nine rebounds. The show said he is on a huge hot streak, top 15 over the last two weeks, and it expects him to cool off.
Oso Ighodaro has started each of Phoenix's last four games. The show said he is not moving out of that starting spot right now, which makes him a usable but risky stream.
Oso Ighodaro stayed in the starting lineup on 11/23 and played 30 minutes. The show said his defensive stats are improving and that he keeps Khaman Maluach from being useful.
Coach Taylor Jenkins said Dieng had successful surgery on a fractured left finger and is expected back in the near term.

Washington missed his first game of the season Saturday with an illness, so Caleb Martin started and Max Christie played 24 minutes and closed the win. Dallas plays at Utah on the second night of a back-to-back and has not posted today's report.
The show said P.J. Washington is listed as questionable for 11/24 with an illness. He missed Dallas's games on 11/21 and 11/22.

Washington is questionable at Denver with the illness that kept him out of Dallas's last two games. When he sat, Zaccharie Risacher started and Daniel Gafford played 31 and 28 minutes, and Dereck Lively II remains out after foot surgery.

Paolo Banchero is out again, and Jalen Suggs and Tristan da Silva (left calf strain) are questionable against Milwaukee. Franz Wagner has played 38 to 40 minutes and topped 50 DraftKings points in each of his last four games.
Paolo Banchero (ankle) is out again at Boston, along with Jonathan Isaac, Noah Penda and Izaiyah Nelson. Franz Wagner has played 36 to 39 minutes in each of his last three games without him.

Banchero has not played since October 23, and November 29 is listed as his earliest possible return. The show said that date will not happen and estimated at least two more weeks, noting he has not yet been reported doing three-on-three or five-on-five work.

Banchero is out again and has not played since Oct. 23. Anthony Black has started and played 35 to 37 minutes in Orlando's last three games, while Tristan da Silva has come off the bench since Jalen Suggs returned.
Pascal Siakam has scored 28 or more points in three of his last four games. The show said he has been especially good offensively lately, though it called Wednesday's matchup a tough spot.
Siakam is questionable at New York with hip soreness, and Indiana is already without Tyrese Haliburton and T.J. McConnell, which would push more minutes to Obi Toppin and Jarace Walker if he sits.

Caleb Wilson has not played since November 11, and the show said he is out with a hand injury. The show said Williams has been starting in his place, but the box scores show he came off the bench on November 13 and 14 while Norman Powell and Zach Collins started. Williams played 24 and 26 minutes in those two games, which is about the same as his minutes before Wilson went down.

Patrick Williams has played 24 to 28 minutes off the bench in his last four games. The show said Caleb Wilson's broken hand opens up more minutes, and that Williams could hold about 25 minutes a night over the next month while Wilson is out.

The show said Patrick Williams got hurt on 11/16 and has since fallen into an 18-to-20-minute role. He had played 24 to 28 minutes per game before that injury, but he has played 13 to 23 minutes in the five games since.
Paul George returned to Boston's starting lineup and played 25 minutes. His return, along with Jordan Walsh starting, sent Luka Garza and Baylor Scheierman to the bench.
Paul George fouled out after 23 minutes in the loss at Denver. The show said he still produced four defensive stats despite the foul trouble.

George is off Boston's injury report after sitting the second night of the back-to-back on Sunday, so he should start at Washington. That likely sends Sam Hauser back to the bench, while Mitchell Robinson (illness) is out again and Neemias Queta keeps the center job.
Paul Reed has played 20 to 28 minutes off the bench in Detroit's last four games. The show said he has earned a role of about 25 minutes, which might fall to about 20 when Jalen Duren returns.

Paul Reed and John Collins are splitting the Detroit center minutes while Jalen Duren is out, with each playing about 25 minutes a game lately. Reed came off the bench for 26 minutes on 11/22 while Collins started and played 22. The show said Reed is the better play because he brings more rebounds, steals and blocks, and that Duren is expected back in about a week.
Paul Reed was listed as a top-100 season-long pickup with Jalen Duren out. Reed played 26 minutes in his last game on 11/22.

The show said Detroit is playing only one big at a time, so Paul Reed and John Collins are not sharing the floor much. Reed has come off the bench but played more minutes than Collins in four of the last six games. The show preferred Reed over Collins.
He is questionable Friday at Charlotte with an eye problem, and the show said Jayson Tatum is expected back after missing Wednesday.
Payton Pritchard went back to the bench after starting the previous game, because Jayson Tatum and Derrick White returned from rest. He scored 5 points in 28 minutes.

Payton Pritchard went back to the bench on Nov. 22 when Jayson Tatum and Derrick White returned, and he took only eight shots in 28 minutes. The show said his shot volume drops when Boston is healthy and that Mike Conley is now taking some of his minutes. The show does not expect him to return to last season's level.
He is questionable tonight vs DET.
Pelle Larsson returned from an illness and started, but he played only 15 minutes. The show said he picked up five fouls, which limited his time.

Pelle Larsson played 15 minutes in a 7-point win against MIL on Wednesday, 14 under his average over his previous 5 games, and sat most of the 8 minutes of garbage time. His 10.5 DraftKings points likely undersell his normal role.

The show said Larsson missed a few games with an illness and has been playing about 28 minutes a night, with foul trouble and early exits cutting into some games. He returned on Nov 18 but played only 15 minutes in that game.

Pelle Larsson started for Miami with Giannis Antetokounmpo out and scored 21 points with three steals and three threes in 30 minutes on 11/22. The show said Larsson moves from borderline to startable while Giannis is out, and it assumes Giannis is out only for a short time.

Pete Nance started and played 28 minutes on November 19 with Kyle Kuzma and Myles Turner both out. He had played only four minutes in his previous appearance on November 11. The show did not see much in the start beyond noting it.

Peyton Watson slid to power forward with Evan Mobley out and played 29 minutes with 15 points and three threes on 11/20. He missed the 11/18 game, which the show tied to a low back bruise, after earlier hamstring soreness. The show said he is above the start line while Mobley is out but is hard to trust to stay healthy.
Peyton Watson blocked six shots in 29 minutes as a starter with Evan Mobley out. The show said he is a strong DFS value with Mobley sidelined.

Washington is questionable for Dallas at Denver, and the show said the news may not come until about 9:30 p.m. Eastern. The show liked him at $5,600 if he plays, and it said his minutes would go to Santi Aldama, Morez Johnson Jr. or Zaccharie Risacher if he sits.
He is questionable tonight at DEN.
Precious Achiuwa returned and played just eight bench minutes. The show said his bigger minutes earlier came while he was filling in for multiple injured players.

Grimes has started with Austin Reaves out and played 37, 42 and 35 minutes in his last three games, including 47 points on 11/17. The show said his value would drop if Reaves returns, especially with the Lakers playing only two games over the next seven nights.

Quentin Grimes has started and played 35 to 42 minutes a night with Austin Reaves out. The show said to hold Grimes for at least one more game, but it expects his value to drop when Reaves returns because he was not valuable in past games alongside Reaves.

Grimes has started and played 35 to 42 minutes in every game since Austin Reaves went out, including 47 points with 10 threes on Nov. 17. The show said Grimes is a must-start whenever Luka Doncic or Reaves is out, but it warned that his lows will be very poor when the Lakers are healthy. The show said Reaves has no concrete timetable to return.
Dan Besbris said to keep rolling Grimes despite a bad shooting night. He has started every game with Austin Reaves out and played 30 to 35 minutes in each of his last three.

Quenton Jackson got another start at point guard with Andrew Nembhard and Tyrese Haliburton both out, scoring 15 points in 22 minutes. The show said he is startable while both are out, but T.J. McConnell (18 minutes, 14 points) caps his upside.

Quenton Jackson started on November 15 and November 18 while Andrew Nembhard was out and played 30 and 22 minutes. With Nembhard back on November 20, he went back to the bench and played 18 minutes. The show said he is a must-start pickup whenever Nembhard sits and noted that Rick Carlisle rarely leans on T.J. McConnell.
Quenton Jackson scored 2 points in 17 minutes as Braden Smith played more and Jalen Slawson entered the rotation. The show said Jackson is a drop candidate in 12-team leagues.

Reed Sheppard played 26 minutes off the bench on November 15 with Fred VanVleet resting and Marcus Smart suspended, up from 13 to 21 minutes in recent games. The show said this was a narrow window because VanVleet is expected to play the next several games, and Smart's suspension will be over by Houston's next back-to-back at the end of November. VanVleet returned on November 16 and Sheppard went back to 19 minutes.
Reed Sheppard played only 19 minutes on 11/16 because Fred VanVleet returned after missing the prior game, when Sheppard had played 26. Marcus Smart was also out on a suspension.

Reed Sheppard scored 20 points in 25 bench minutes, but the show said his minutes are not safe at roughly 20 a game. The show noted his best games have come in back-to-backs when Fred VanVleet or Marcus Smart sat, and an injury to Tari Eason would be the fastest path to more playing time.
Reed Sheppard played only 14 minutes on Friday, Nov. 20, down from about 22 in his previous five games, in a close game where Houston leaned on its starters and the bench scored 12 points.

Barrett took at least 16 shots in each game while Scottie Barnes was out, but he took only 11 shots on November 15 when Barnes returned. The show said Barrett is hard to play at $8,000 now that Barnes is back.
RJ Barrett missed his third straight game on Monday with a right hamstring injury.

Williams has a steady backup center role of 15 to 17 minutes a night. The show said his best games come when the starter ahead of him gets into foul trouble, because that is when his blocks and rebounds pile up.

Grayson Allen was out on Nov. 17, which let O'Neale play 34 minutes off the bench after he had played 18 to 26 minutes in his earlier games. The show called his production in that larger role decidedly meh.
Royce O'Neale played 21 minutes off the bench on 11/20. The show said he is the most likely player to move into the Hornets' starting lineup if Brandon Miller misses time with his ankle sprain.

The show said Minnesota's offense without Anthony Edwards has become fast-moving and built around LaMelo Ball, which leaves Gobert as a poor fit. It said his rebounding is down and that Chris Finch criticized him for not holding onto the ball. Gobert had 0 points and 4 rebounds in 22 minutes on 11/17 and 9 points with 7 rebounds in 35 minutes on 11/19.
The show said it was encouraging that Rudy Gobert played 35 minutes, but he had only nine points, seven rebounds and no blocks. The show called his production frustrating.

Rudy Gobert played 32 minutes on 11/21 and had 11 rebounds, three blocks and a steal on 2-of-2 shooting. Backup Joan Beringer played 16 minutes and did not score. The show said Gobert's numbers have been underwhelming this season but his minutes and role remain secure.

Rudy Gobert has scored single digits in four of Minnesota's last five games while still starting. Joan Beringer has played 13 to 26 minutes off the bench in this stretch. The show said it feels like Beringer will eventually push Gobert out of the way.

Rui Hachimura played 22 minutes as a starter on November 15 and was a minus 11 while the Clippers' bench carried the game. The show said he is shooting about 36.5 percent from the field and 68 percent from the line this season. The show said he is hurting fantasy teams despite good underlying numbers.

Rui Hachimura scored 17 points with seven rebounds as a starter, but the show said it is not enough to hold him. The show said Hachimura could be the one who moves to the bench when Brandon Ingram returns.

Rui Hachimura played 32 minutes and scored 17 points at San Antonio, after 27 minutes and 20 points on November 17. The show said he is finally playing more like it expected with Brandon Ingram out, but it is not sure the run will last.

The show said Rui Hachimura's usage is way up this season compared with his past years, but his poor shooting has kept his fantasy value down. He played 32 minutes as a starter and took 13 shots in this game. The show expects his value to rise if his field goal and free throw shooting return to normal.

Ryan Conwell played 33 and 26 minutes off the bench in Miami's last two games, more than Andrew Wiggins and Bobby Portis, and he scored 20 points on November 13 when Pelle Larsson and Klay Thompson were out. The show said he is basically playing a sixth-man role and sometimes closes games, and it would grab him everywhere if Davion Mitchell got hurt.
Ryan Conwell has played 26 to 33 minutes off the bench in Miami's last three games while Myron Gardner has started. The show said Conwell has been productive even without shooting well.
The show said Conwell is now Miami's sixth man and is playing better than Andrew Wiggins and Bobby Portis right now. Conwell has played between 21 and 33 minutes in each of his last six games.

Ryan Conwell played 29 minutes off the bench while Giannis Antetokounmpo was out. The show said it likes him but that he does not usually play enough to be worth rostering, and it attributed the minutes to players being unavailable.

Kalkbrenner started on Nov 6 and Nov 9 while Moussa Diabate was out, and he played 35 minutes with 15 rebounds on Nov 9. Diabate returned on Nov 12, and Kalkbrenner has come off the bench for 16 to 18 minutes since then. The show said Kalkbrenner produces whenever Diabate misses.

Rollins missed two games with an illness, and when he returned on Nov 19 he played only 21 minutes off the bench after logging 29 minutes in his previous game. The show said the main thing blocking his role is rookie Brayden Burries, whom the Bucks are invested in as a starter, with Kasparas Jakucionis also playing over him at times. In the next game on Nov 21, however, Rollins started and played 28 minutes while Burries came off the bench.

Ryan Rollins had his best game of the season off the bench with 15 points, six assists and four steals, but he played only 21 minutes. The show said young players like Brayden Burries and Nate Ament are blocking his path to more minutes. The show said his way back is becoming the high-usage bench guard in a tighter rotation.
He is questionable tonight vs POR.

The show said Ryan Rollins has been a major disappointment and that it is watching whether this is a slump or a real drop from last season. In the box scores he is averaging about 24 minutes per game, splitting guard minutes with rookies Brayden Burries (about 23) and Kasparas Jakucionis (about 19) behind Tyler Herro, and he started on Nov 10 and Nov 21.

Ryan Rollins moved back into the starting lineup on Nov. 21 and Nov. 23 when Milwaukee went with a bigger group of Kyle Kuzma, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Myles Turner and Tyler Herro. He played 28 and then 22 minutes in those starts. The show said Brayden Burries is outplaying him and that the team may start to favor its youth.

Rollins has bounced between the bench and the starting lineup, playing 21 to 29 minutes over his last five games. The show said his minutes can go anywhere and Toronto's slow pace and good defense hurt him, so it listed him as a fade at 20 percent ownership.

Saddiq Bey started and played 33 to 42 minutes in every game while Trey Murphy III was out. The show worried his minutes and usage would drop when Murphy returned, but Bey still started and played 37 minutes when Murphy came back on November 20.

Saddiq Bey has started every recent game, but he scored only 2 points on 12 shots in 32 minutes on 11/21. The show said New Orleans may move Bey to the bench so Trey Murphy III can start again now that the team is getting healthier.

Bey has started six straight games for New Orleans and has played 32 to 42 minutes, with Trey Murphy III and Dejounte Murray both missing time. The show said he is getting a ton of usage and has a solid rebounding and assist floor. Murphy returned off the bench on Nov. 20, so Bey's role should be watched.
Saddiq Bey was listed as a top-100 season-long pickup with Dejounte Murray out. Bey played 32 minutes in his last game on 11/21.
Saddiq Bey came off the bench on Monday with Trey Murphy III back in the lineup but still played 40 minutes in the overtime loss to Phoenix.

Hauser started and played 31 minutes on 11/21 while Jayson Tatum and Derrick White rested on the back-to-back. The show said he was only a short-term stream for that weekend. Tatum and White returned on 11/22, Paul George rested instead, and Hauser fell to 22 minutes.

Sam Hauser started Boston's last two games, but the show expects him to go back to the bench on Tuesday with Paul George returning. The show projected him for about 21 to 22 minutes with three-point upside.

Sam Merrill played 25 minutes off the bench on 11/20 in his second game back from injury. The show said his minutes are coming out of Tyrese Proctor's share rather than from Harden, Mitchell, Watson or Allen.
Sam Merrill moved into Cleveland's starting lineup on 11/23, replacing Tyrese Proctor, and played 25 minutes. The show called him a three-point streamer.

Sandro Mamukelashvili fell to 21 minutes and four points on November 15 after scoring 23 points in each of his two previous games. Those big games came while Quentin Grimes was unavailable, and Grimes returned to start this one. The show said the Lakers have one or two too many wing players, so the safest move is to trust the starters.

Walker Kessler rested on 11/17, but Mamukelashvili did not benefit, going 1-of-8 for three points in 23 bench minutes. The show said he had been the bench player Luka Doncic looked for most, but Quentin Grimes took that role in this game. The show called him a streaming option only after two straight poor games.
Mamukelashvili played 21 minutes and scored six points on 10 percent shooting. The show said he has no path to big minutes and did not even start when Walker Kessler was out.
Aldama returned Wednesday from a left ankle sprain that cost him Sunday's game, but played only six minutes.

Scoot Henderson played 35 minutes off the bench and scored 27 points on November 19 with Deni Avdija out, after playing 19 to 23 minutes in most recent games. With Avdija back on November 21 he returned to 23 minutes, and the show said it is hard to trust him nightly because he has been inefficient and Ja Morant will eventually return.

Scoot Henderson played 23 minutes and scored 3 points on 11/21 after scoring 27 in 35 minutes on 11/19. His minutes fell back to his usual range with Deni Avdija returning from his absence. The show said his big game was not a sign of a new role.

Scottie Barnes has missed three straight games with a groin strain, and Toronto is on the second night of a back-to-back at Philadelphia. Immanuel Quickley returned Wednesday and played 28 minutes; the Raptors have not posted tonight's report yet.
He is questionable tonight vs NYK.

Toronto hosts New York again two nights after an overtime loss in which Scottie Barnes returned from a groin strain and played 36 minutes. Kawhi Leonard is out again (left knee injury management), and New York has nobody on the injury report.

Barnes is off the injury report after sitting Wednesday with a groin issue, but RJ Barrett will be re-evaluated in two weeks (hamstring) and Collin Murray-Boyles is in the concussion protocol, so Toronto's offense runs through Barnes at Detroit.
The show credited Scottie Barnes with 32% usage over 38 minutes on 11/23 with RJ Barrett and Kawhi Leonard out. The show called him a possible sell-high because Leonard will return at some point.
Scotty Pippen Jr. is week-to-week with a lumbar disc herniation and has not played since October 29, with no firm return date. Cam Spencer moved into the starting lineup in his place.
The show said Sergio de Larrea will miss at least another week with a sprained knee, and he has not played since Oct. 26.
He scored 43 points with eight assists in 39 minutes Monday against Cleveland and faces the same team again with Chet Holmgren, Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace all out.
Oklahoma City is without Chet Holmgren, Jalen Williams, Cason Wallace and Jaylin Williams at Portland, which is missing Ja Morant and Shaedon Sharpe. This late game is off the main slate.

Shai Gilgeous-Alexander scored 40 points in 37 minutes on 11/20 with Chet Holmgren, Jalen Williams, Alex Caruso and Cason Wallace all out. The show said he is going to have to do a lot moving forward.

Gilgeous-Alexander is questionable at Miami with a low back contusion and a neck strain after scoring 40 on Friday. Oklahoma City is already without Chet Holmgren, Jalen Williams, Alex Caruso, Cason Wallace and Nikola Topic.

Shai Gilgeous-Alexander returned on 11/23 and went back into the starting lineup in place of Kenrich Williams, not Micah Peavy. The show is concerned that his drop in shooting efficiency may be lasting.

Oklahoma City is missing Jalen Williams, Chet Holmgren, Alex Caruso, Cason Wallace, Jaylin Williams and several others. The show said Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Ajay Mitchell and Isaiah Hartenstein are the only locks, while the rest of the rotation is a dice roll with Jared McCain as a scorer and Kenrich Williams as an all-around option.
Shai Gilgeous-Alexander played 38 minutes on Monday and carried a short-handed Thunder team, which kept the game close until the final minute.

Gilgeous-Alexander missed his first game of the season Sunday at Miami with a neck strain and a lower back contusion, and Oklahoma City played with only nine players. The Thunder had not filed today's report this morning, so his status at Indiana is not posted.
Sidy Cissoko started over Scoot Henderson in Tuesday's 123-103 win over Oklahoma City and scored 17 points in 33 minutes. The same teams meet again tonight in Portland.
Sidy Cissoko started and played 31 minutes with Deni Avdija out. The show said it is not interested in Cissoko for fantasy despite the role.

Sidy Cissoko has started every game and played 31 and 32 minutes in Portland's last two games with Deni Avdija out. The show likes him as a deep-league streamer because of that steady 30-minute floor and his steals upside.
Sidy Cissoko has started Portland's recent games with Ja Morant out with a hamstring strain. The show said he could play 30 minutes as a starter and has been getting solid run.
The show said Sidy Cissoko will stay in the Blazers starting lineup until Ja Morant returns from his hamstring strain. Cissoko has started every recent game and played 24 minutes on Nov. 23.

Sion James is starting for Charlotte and played 32 and 35 minutes in his last two games. The show said he does not put up big numbers but can add steals, threes and some assists with that playing time.
Sion James came off the bench Tuesday after starting Charlotte's previous three games, with Grant Williams starting, and played 30 minutes.
Spencer Jones has held a reserve role of about 17 to 21 minutes for Denver. The show described him as a low-volume, efficient player who adds steals and rebounds in that role.

Stephen Curry is out with a right oblique tear, and Jimmy Butler, Kristaps Porzingis, Moses Moody and Brandon Williams are out as well for the game at San Antonio. Yaxel Lendeborg (36 minutes) and Brandin Podziemski (37 minutes) carried the offense Wednesday after Curry went down.

Stephen Curry has no timeline for his right oblique tear; Steve Kerr said Sunday they will know more in two weeks. Brandon Williams' hamstring is taking longer than expected, Kristaps Porzingis is away from the team, and Gui Santos is questionable with a new ankle injury.
He is ruled out tonight (right oblique tear). Podziemski steps up.

Curry has missed four straight games with an oblique tear and Draymond Green sat Thursday with a right elbow injury. Golden State finished its road trip 0-5 with a 12th different starting lineup, and Charles Bassey has started the last two games at center.
Curry was still out on Sunday, Nov. 22, and Golden State used its seventh starting lineup in seven games and its 13th of the season.

Stephon Castle played 35 minutes with De'Aaron Fox out and had 20 points, nine assists and four steals. The show said Fox's absence helped and that it was his second strong game in a row after a slump.

The show said Harper has been one of the higher-usage Spurs alongside Victor Wembanyama and Castle. With Harper out for what could be weeks, the show expected Castle and De'Aaron Fox to benefit the most from the extra usage.

With Dylan Harper out, Stephon Castle handled the offense for 33 minutes on November 19 and had 12 assists with eight turnovers against the Clippers. The show said Castle could have a big two-week run with Harper sidelined and De'Aaron Fox banged up.

With Dylan Harper out, Stephon Castle had 19 points and 6 assists, De'Aaron Fox had 10 assists, Julian Champagnie hit 3 threes with a block, and Devin Vassell blocked 2 shots. The show said all of those Spurs are playable in any game where Victor Wembanyama does not dominate the workload.

With Victor Wembanyama, De'Aaron Fox and Dylan Harper all out on Monday, Stephon Castle ran the Spurs offense for 37 minutes and had 11 assists. He scored nine straight points during the third-quarter run that broke the game open.

Steven Adams started for Houston on November 15 in only his second game of the season, and he played 12 minutes. The show said Houston started him so he could guard Anthony Davis and keep Davis from attacking Alperen Sengun.
Steven Adams is probable to return from a right soleus strain that has kept him to one game this season, with Clint Capela still out.
Steven Adams rested on the second night of Houston's back-to-back, and Amen Thompson was also out. The show expects Adams back for the next game.
Adams opened the second half at center Wednesday after Alperen Sengun left with an eye injury, and played 16 minutes. He would be next in line if Sengun misses time.

Mykhailiuk played 33 and 34 minutes off the bench on 11/17 and 11/18, with five assists in both games. On 11/18, Darryn Peterson played only 19 minutes and Brice Sensabaugh played only 14. The show said it did not know why Utah turned to him, and he played 28 minutes on 11/20.
Mykhailiuk has played 33, 34 and 28 minutes in Utah's last three games off the bench. The show said the role might not stick, but it noted that Will Hardy relied on him heavily last season.

Svi Mykhailiuk played at least 28 minutes off the bench in four straight Jazz games from Nov. 17 to Nov. 22, and that run ended with 39 points and 10 threes in 32 minutes against Dallas. The show said it would choose him over Brice Sensabaugh because his minutes are steady, although he dropped to 25 minutes and four points on Nov. 23.

McConnell scored 27 DraftKings points in 18 bench minutes on 11/18. The show said he is most productive in his roughly 20-minute role and that his output tends to flatten out when he gets extended to 25 minutes.
T.J. McConnell is probable Wednesday (hamstring) and his minutes have been rising over his five games since his season debut on November 7, with Tyrese Haliburton out.

Tari Eason played 23 minutes off the bench on 11/20, which is down from 30 and 33 minutes earlier in the month. The show said it worries about his limited role but would still hold him because he is one injury away from a bigger role.
Tari Eason played 22 minutes off the bench on 11/23. The show said he needs a teammate out to reach his upside.
Tarris Reed Jr. got the backup center minutes on 11/23 with Victor Wembanyama out and played 15 minutes.

Taylor Hendricks started at center with Zach Edey out, and Isaiah Stewart came off the bench instead of starting. The show said neither Hendricks at 20 minutes nor Stewart at 18 minutes played enough to matter for fantasy.

Hendricks started on 11/19, when Jerami Grant played only 5 minutes. On 11/21 Zach Edey started, Boozer was out, and Hendricks went to the bench for 27 minutes with 5 points. The show said that made him an easy drop.

The show said Taylor Hendricks is the Memphis player whose value rises most with Cameron Boozer out because he can play as a wing, a four or a small-ball center. The show ranked him ahead of Isaiah Stewart and also called him the top stream whenever Zach Edey misses. Hendricks has played 19 to 29 minutes in each game since 11/13.

The show said Taylor Hendricks is the first forward to pick up minutes while Cameron Boozer, Jerami Grant and GG Jackson are out, with Olivier-Maxence Prosper as the deeper option. Boozer missed his second straight game on Nov. 23 with a right ankle sprain, and Hendricks played 27 and 24 minutes off the bench in those two games while Prosper played 23 and 19.
Shannon scored 34 points in 35 minutes on 11/16 and followed with 24 minutes on 11/17. The show said his role has been fairly consistent and that he always has a pop-off game in him.
Terrence Shannon Jr. has played 21 to 35 minutes off the bench with Anthony Edwards out. The show said he gets 21 to 22 minutes and is a streaming option but not a must-roster player.

Shannon has been a key bench scorer for Minnesota with Anthony Edwards out with a knee injury, as Edwards has not played since October 26. After his 34-point game on November 16, he has settled in at 21 to 26 minutes and scored 12, 10 and 15 points. The show said he should keep delivering steady value for as long as Edwards stays sidelined.

The show said Terrence Shannon Jr. is still coming off the bench with Anthony Edwards out, which has made his production inconsistent, but it called him a good short-term hot-hand stream. He has played 21 to 26 minutes off the bench in most games since 11/12, with a 35-minute game on 11/16.
Thomas Bryant started at center and played 27 minutes on Saturday, November 14, because Jarrett Allen and Evan Mobley were both ruled out.
Thomas Bryant started on November 14 only because Jarrett Allen and Evan Mobley were both out. Allen is not on Monday's injury report, so Bryant should return to backup center against Chicago.

Thomas Sorber underwent a right knee arthroscopy for patellofemoral joint inflammation that developed during his rehab. The show reported that he will return to on-court activities in six to eight weeks, so he is not a factor for the Thunder in the near term.
Tobias Harris remains out with a left calf strain. The show said San Antonio announced that he will come off the bench when he returns.
Harris is out with a left calf strain. The show said this is the first weekly preview in which it does not expect him to return during the coming week.

Bradley is Utah's backup center behind Mo Bamba with the other centers out, and he has played 12 to 14 minutes in each of his last three games. The show said he does not project well, but he has the most natural path to extra minutes if Bamba gets hurt or cannot stay on the floor.

Camara played 37 minutes with Deni Avdija out on 11/19 and broke a shooting slump with 18 points, four threes, two steals and three blocks. He had scored 3 and 10 points in his two games before that. The show said Avdija's absence helped, but it believes Camara has value on his own when Avdija returns.
The show said Wednesday is Trae Young's first game against his former team, Atlanta.

Trae Young is in a deep shooting slump, but he has kept playing 32 to 33 minutes as Washington's starter, and the team snapped a long losing streak. The show said his minutes and shots are not wavering, so it expects his efficiency to bounce back.
Trae Young played only 28 minutes in a blowout win and sat the late fourth quarter. The show noted that Washington had him play off the ball a lot, and his usage was only about 23 percent.

Trae Young played 28 minutes in a 20-point win against ORL on Sunday, 6 under his average over his previous 5 games, and sat most of the 8 minutes of garbage time. His 36.0 DraftKings points likely undersell his normal role.

The show said Trae Young's usage drops to about 20.5 percent when AJ Dybantsa is on the floor. It said Young seems to be deferring since Dybantsa returned, is barely getting to the free-throw line, and is playing more like a $6,500 player than his $7,200 price.

The show said Bub Carrington is back out of the rotation, and Carrington played only two minutes. That gave Tre Johnson the backup point guard minutes, and he scored nine points in 21 minutes, which the show called a score-only role.

Johnson played only eight minutes and did not score on Wednesday, after playing about 30 minutes as recently as Nov. 12. The show called him a bust so far and said Will Riley is also back in the rotation but playing poorly.

Tre Jones has come off the bench in every recent game and played 24, 23 and 16 minutes over the Bulls' last three games. The show reviewed the Bulls' rotation and said Jones subs in directly for Josh Giddey with almost no shared minutes, so his playing time is capped while Giddey plays. The show said it likes Jones more when Giddey is not available.

The show said Jones is taking minutes from Josh Giddey because Giddey is struggling and coach Tiago Splitter is quick to pull him. Jones played 25 minutes on November 20 while Giddey played only 23 minutes and scored two points. The show added that Jones can reach 26 minutes on nights he starts and that Chicago plays three games in four nights.

Jones has come off the bench in every recent Bulls game at anywhere from 14 to 28 minutes, and he still produced 10 points and six assists in 16 minutes on Nov. 18. The show said he becomes useful if his role grows to 25 to 30 minutes per night.
Jones did not grab the extra role when Norman Powell sat on November 22 and played only 12 minutes off the bench. The show said he did not take his opportunity because Josh Giddey played so well.
Tre Jones played 27 minutes off the bench on Monday as Chicago spread out minutes the night after an overtime game, and he had nine assists while Josh Giddey was held to 22 minutes.

Trevon Brazile has played only 11 to 15 minutes in his last three games after early-season hype. The show said his minutes are nowhere near where they were when Denver was missing wings, though he is still a good rebounder.

Lyles played 31 minutes off the bench on 11/17 with Jonathan Kuminga out, while Cody Williams got the start but played only 13 minutes. The show said Lyles is the one who got the big minutes and is a watch-list player if Kuminga's injury lasts.
The show said he should be back Friday against Minnesota after missing Wednesday with knee soreness.

Trey Murphy III, Bennedict Mathurin, Yves Missi and Bryce McGowens are all doubtful and Trendon Watford is out for New Orleans. Zion Williamson scored 29 in 30 minutes in his return Wednesday, and Jeremiah Fears, Saddiq Bey and Jordan Poole should soak up the open wing minutes.

Trey Murphy III is averaging about 32 minutes per game in the box scores, down from about 35 last season, and the show said his usage has fallen from 23% to about 18.5%. The show said his catch-and-shoot three-point attempts dropped from 5.1 to 3.8 per game even though he is still making them at a high rate, and it blamed the coaching staff for not running plays to get him those looks. The show also said the Pelicans sharing the ball with Dejounte Murray, Jeremiah Fears and Zion Williamson is part of it, and that a Murray trade could bring back another player who takes shots.

Trey Murphy III returned Friday after six missed games and played 29 minutes off the bench, and Jordan Poole's minutes fell to 13. New Orleans has not posted its injury report for the back-to-back yet.
Trey Murphy III started and played 35 minutes on Monday as he works back from knee soreness that sidelined him for seven of New Orleans' previous eight games. He looked rusty, shooting 4 of 14.
Trey Murphy III returned to the starting lineup on 11/23 and played 35 minutes, but he had only 18% usage. The show said Saddiq Bey is taking too many of his shots and called Murphy a buy-low.

Tristan da Silva played 24 minutes off the bench on 11/20 with Paolo Banchero still out, which is down from 31 and 27 minutes in recent games. The show said he only has value while Banchero is out and becomes a streaming option once Banchero returns.
Tristan da Silva has played 24 to 31 minutes in every recent game, mostly off the bench. The show said his minutes are relatively safe and his value comes from three-pointers.

Tristan da Silva moved to the bench when Jalen Suggs returned to the lineup on 11/16. He has played 24 to 31 minutes off the bench since then, and the show called him a playable sixth man under $5,000.

Ty Jerome missed his third straight game Wednesday with right hip soreness, and Memphis had not filed for tonight. Cam Spencer has started in his place and scored 26 as the Grizzlies set a franchise record with their eighth straight road win.

Ty Jerome played 27 minutes in his return on November 21. The show expects him to get back up to about 30 minutes, but it warned that Memphis has been unpredictable with minutes. His return also cuts into the role Javon Small had been filling.
Ty Jerome is Memphis's leading scorer this season, and with Cameron Boozer out he took 21 shots in 29 minutes on Monday.
He is questionable with a right contusion at New York, and Josh Hart is questionable for the Knicks with right ankle soreness. New York is a 16.5-point favorite.

Tyler Herro missed Tuesday's 32-point loss at New York with a bruised right knee, his first missed game of the season. Milwaukee hosts the Lakers on the second night of a back-to-back, and its injury report is not posted yet.

Tyler Herro played only 20 minutes and scored five points on 13 shots. The show said his minutes were cut because he played poorly, and it thought he was immune to Milwaukee's rotation randomness but now is less sure.
The show said Tyler Herro looks like he has given up, after being the one Buck who seemed to be trying hard for the first three weeks. He scored eight points in 24 minutes on Wednesday.

Tyler Herro played 24 minutes in a 7-point loss against MIA on Wednesday, 6 under his average over his previous 5 games, and sat most of the 8 minutes of garbage time. His 18.5 DraftKings points likely undersell his normal role.

items.text: Washington is questionable at Denver with the illness that kept him out of Dallas's last two games. When he sat, Zaccharie Risacher started and Daniel Gafford played 31 and 28 minutes, and Dereck Lively II remains out after foot surgery.

George is off Boston's injury report after sitting the second night of the back-to-back on Sunday, so he should start at Washington. That likely sends Sam Hauser back to the bench, while Mitchell Robinson (illness) is out again and Neemias Queta keeps the center job.

Duren (hamstring) and Duncan Robinson (quadriceps) are both out again at Orlando, and Cade Cunningham is probable with knee soreness. John Collins starts at center, Paul Reed splits those minutes off the bench, and Isaiah Joe played 26 minutes on Sunday.

Banchero is out again and has not played since Oct. 23. Anthony Black has started and played 35 to 37 minutes in Orlando's last three games, while Tristan da Silva has come off the bench since Jalen Suggs returned.
Ingram made his Clippers debut on Monday after sitting out since May following heel and Achilles surgery. He started and played 27 minutes in his first game back.
Wembanyama sat Monday with back tightness, and De'Aaron Fox (shin) and Dylan Harper (hip) were also out. Stephon Castle ran the offense for 37 minutes with 11 assists in the win at Sacramento.

Giddey played only 22 minutes on Monday, the night after his 22-assist overtime game against Denver, because the Bulls spread out playing time on the back-to-back. Tre Jones played 27 minutes off the bench.
Boozer is expected to miss at least a month with a sprained right ankle. Ty Jerome took 21 shots in 29 minutes in the first game without him.
